candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: On Vasu’s admission, Paresh and Prabhav have debtors of ₹6,20,000 and an existing provision for doubtful debts of ₹20,000. Debtors worth ₹15,000 have turned bad and must be written off. Which entries correctly record this write-off?

options.text: Bad Debts A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Debtors A/c ₹15,000. Then Provision for Doubtful Debts A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Bad Debts A/c ₹15,000.
Bad Debts A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Debtors A/c ₹15,000. Then Revaluation A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Provision for Doubtful Debts A/c ₹15,000.
Revaluation A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Debtors A/c ₹15,000.
Bad Debts A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Revaluation A/c ₹15,000.

candidate.explanation: The existing 20000 provision covers the 15000 write-off. Debit Bad Debts and credit Debtors; then debit the provision and credit Bad Debts. Remaining provision is 5000 and net debtor value stays 600000; no new revaluation loss is invented. A: Matches the write-off and its adjustment against the existing provision. B: Creates or increases a provision through Revaluation instead of consuming the existing provision. C: Charges a new revaluation loss while leaving the covering provision unadjusted. D: Does not credit debtors and improperly credits Revaluation.

oracle.basis: A CBSE-reference practice adaptation cannot claim an authenticated CUET PYQ anchor.
